arms.original: Historical raw full image; replay must be bitwise exact.
arms.reviewed_crop: Human box plus fixed5percent padding, EXIF display orientation; replay must match current corrected crop cache.
arms.raw_orientation_crop: Same reviewed crop pixels, inverse EXIF orientation only; reuse reviewed_crop if orientation1.
arms.context_gray: Full original processor grid; replace only patches entirely outside the padded box with neutral gray. Retained patch values and indices unchanged.
arms.context_white: Same as context_gray, white fill control.
arms.native_patch_crop: Extract the retained rectangular patch block from original processor input; no resizing and identical patch values. Grid/positions/sequence change.
arms.enlarged_patch_crop: Upsample that identical low-resolution patch block to the standard processor crop budget. Adds no original-image detail; changes scale/grid and interpolated samples.

comparisons: reviewed_crop vs raw_orientation_crop: pixel orientation control
original vs context_gray/white at fixed retained readout: outside-patch context intervention
context_gray/white retained readout vs native_patch_crop: sequence/grid/position and excluded-context-token changes at identical retained pixels
native_patch_crop vs enlarged_patch_crop: resampling plus scale/grid; no added source detail
all_tokens vs subject_plus_template within the same encoded image: readout intervention
control_selection: One unique success control per harm; minimize identity mismatch, orientation mismatch, background mismatch, log subject-area gap, then queryID. No intervention outcome used.
limits: Diagnostic selected cohort; not a population accuracy claim or held-out repair tuning.
Human boxes are rectangles, not pixel-perfect object segmentation.
Native patch crop rounds crop extent outward to full28pixel visual patches; differs slightly from exact historical crop extent.
Scale and grid/token budget are a joint intervention here; cannot uniquely attribute to optical detail.
Pixel context dependence and score changes do not establish semantic identity content in background pixels.
Reencoding may change contextual representations at retained positions; claim loss of identity only with additional evidence.
